summary: Proceed as a scored combination run. The cache layout and FP8 scale conventions match decode's exactly, and the run time stays well inside 15 minutes. Five build notes are binding: the attention module's ticket arrays move into state; A1's variant and grid are raced or ported, not hard-coded; the race times the qkv GEMM through the o-GEMM input; every A1/A2 gate keeps page_size == 1; and the text must say clearly that this is not all of C1 (S3 c1/c3/c4 are missing), so the headline is not compared with C1 on the full-layer rows.
justification: A. The mechanism is plausible and the run can test the conjecture, because every band prints every candidate's time in the same interleaved replay set and adds the 'PATH CHOSEN' line. In 933d, the sliding batched rows still run the FA3 chain: FA3 13.6/18.2 + combine 4.3/2.9 + prepare_varlen 2.3/2.2 + FusedQKNorm, casts, store_cache and FusedRMSNormGate. That is about 28-30 us of nodes. D1 removed about 9-11 us of it before. Attention's log 252abb7f shows pre + sk variant 6, grid p4, at 19.5 us net against Triton's 25.8 us at B=32. An in-layer margin for A1 over D1 at SB32 is credible, but it will be smaller than 6.3 us, as the conjecture itself predicts. SB1: attention's cluster C=16 kernel row is 10.8 us against _sliding_fused_kernel's 13.2 us in 933d, so roughly -2 us on a 118 us row. That is about 1.7%, close to the selector's 1.02 threshold and to the run's ±1.5% interval, so whatever SB1 decides will not show clearly in the headline. Its race line is the evidence. The expected directions match TASK weights: sliding rows are weighted 46, so sliding decode_32 (the worst ratio, 1.080x) and verify_1 are the leverage points. The headline estimate of +2..2.5% is optimistic. A1 has never run inside decode, and the C1 parts dropped here (below) give up Fd16/Fd32/Fv1 gains that C1 expects. WEAKEST LINK: A1's configuration is pinned from attention's standalone choices and is partly wrong or unspecified. Attention never gated sk-window at B=2..16 (its log says 'master (Triton), not gated in this restack'). No grid spec is given for variant 6 at SB16. For sliding verify B=1, attention's own runs chose single-level variant 4 at grid p8 (logs bd0ddd41, 94523c33), not variant 5 as the hypothesis states. If A1 is entered with the wrong variant or grid, it loses the race for configuration reasons, and the conjecture ('the ranking does not transfer') is then confirmed spuriously. Fix: race A1's own {variant 4/5 (SV1) or 6/7 (decode)} x {p2, p4, p8, sm} with the ported _sd/_ps gate-band code, and enter only its best into the three-way race. Or port attention master's _SD_ROUTE/_PS_ROUTE choices exactly as its log printed them: B=17..32 is variant 6, grid p4. KV/FP8 match (EXTRA_NOTE), verified in code. Both problems use float8_e4m3fn [pages, page_size, 2, 64] contiguous, flat row = cache_loc = page*page_size + offset, row = 2 kv heads x 64 B. Attention's _pre_attention_kernel and the cluster kernel write k at (loc*HKV + kh)*D. Both store k/k_scale and v/v_scale, and both apply score scale sm_scale*qk_scale_factor*log2e*k_scale with output times v_scale, which is decode's convention (key = e4m3 * k_scale). The qkv row layout is identical: q 16x64 | k 2x64 | v 2x64 | gate 16x64, gate at element 1280 = decode's SK_QKV_GATE_OFF = attention's (HQ+2HKV)*D. QK-norm is scaleless in both, the output RMSNorm is scaleless then times sigmoid(gate) in both, and both use interleaved RoPE with theta 500000. Known byte differences: (1) attention normalises k in fp32 and encodes it straight to E4M3, while master rounds through bf16 (FusedQKNorm) first; (2) Triton tl.sin/tl.cos are approximate (LESSONS line 140). Both give a few k bytes off by one E4M3 code, which is what the hypothesis's '< 6% within one code' bound covers and which is far inside the judge's 8% cache bound. v is byte-exact at kv_scale 1 and 1/64 (power-of-two division). The cluster kernel rounds q*qk_scale_factor to E4M3 rather than rounding q and then scaling. That is the same E4M3 precision, so the 'no coarser than E4M3' rule holds, and attention's judge accepted it. BUDGET (EXTRA_NOTE): 933d ran 237.5 s end to end (okc created->finished). Master builds 3 modules at import; sk/splitkv builds in the logs take 30-50 s each. Adding A1, the SK_PSEUDO TU holding all 8 variant instantiations (likely 45-60 s rather than 35), and A2 (about 40 s, plus about 40 s more if its f16 mma fallback build triggers) adds about 85-140 s. With prepare's +50 s, the worst case is about 375-430 s, against 900 s. That is safe with more than 450 s of margin. Prepare's 300 s limit is also safe: master's prepare took 4.5 s, the last phase's start deadline is 200 s, and the race takes about 12 s.
confounders: C1 itself (combo-measured-rows-slide-batched-preattn-t8-tail): this is NOT 'C1 plus attention ports'. It carries C1's S1 (as D1) and S2 (as D2), but S3 only on sliding verify B=1 (D3). C1's S3 c1 (full decode 1<B<=64, +4.7/+3.3% own-base), c2 at T=128/256 (sliding verify_16/32), c3 (full verify B>1) and c4 (full verify_1) are all missing. On Fd16, Fd32, Fv1, Sv16 and Sv32 the two combos therefore differ by S3, not by the race, so a same-day headline comparison with C1 cannot be attributed. The rows that compare cleanly with C1 are Sd1, Sd16, Sd32 and Sv1 only, and then only if C1's S3 c2 selector at T=8 decides the same way as this run's D3 candidate.

small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl / dense-chain-s3 (PDL chain at T<=32): A1's pre + sk and A2's cluster kernel are ported without griddepcontrol. Inserting them between a PDL-launched qkv GEMM and o GEMM can cost the PDL overlap that master's or D1's path keeps. A race that times only the attention kernels would hide this; a race over qkv -> o-GEMM input exposes it. The conjecture's L2-hot claim is likewise only testable if the race graph includes the qkv GEMM with a cold-L2 flush before it.

sliding-decode1-fused-restack-on-pdl (in stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1): this is SB1's incumbent, _sliding_fused_kernel 13.2 us. A2 is raced directly against it, so attribution is clean. But the incumbent fuses RoPE and the cache store and may sit inside the PDL chain, so the head-to-head must run on the same captured neighbours.

full-decode-sk-ticket-restack-b1-b64 / dl3-piece-a: decode's _SK module stays byte-identical and the new module builds the same TU source under a new name. That is harmless only if the tickets are separate per-state arrays (see rules_flags). If the new module reuses attention's module-global _ps_ticket/_ps_gticket, it is a cross-state shared counter. That works while replays are serialized, but it breaks the stated two-state invariant.
interference: No companion is warranted. The run is self-attributing on its four bands: every candidate's time and the winner are printed per band from one interleaved replay set, and the shape rows can be compared with 933d. C1 is already queued from the same mint, so a same-day C1 result serves as the drift reference on Sd1, Sd16, Sd32 and Sv1 at no extra scored cost. An ab-revert of any landed hypothesis would not make either a gain or a loss less ambiguous, because the race already pits master's incumbent against each source inside the same layer. The one ambiguity that matters, A1 losing because its variant or grid was wrong, is fixed by the in-run A1 variant x grid sub-race required in justification, not by another scored run. Optional, no extra run: if the builder adds C1's S3 c1-c4 verbatim (Triton only, no new module), the whole run differs from C1 only by the race, and a full-headline A/B against C1 becomes valid.
rules_flags: Ticket arrays: attention master keeps _TICKETS, _GTICKETS, _PS_TICKETS and _PS_GTICKETS as module-global dicts keyed by device (_sk_ticket/_sk_gticket/_ps_ticket/_ps_gticket). The 'copy verbatim' instruction must NOT carry these over. Allocate state['skw_ticket'] int32[256] and state['skw_gticket'] int32[256*32] per state, zeroed in prepare. Check after each alternation replay that they return to 0, as attention's 'tickets 0' check does. The same applies to D1's state['slide_cnt'], which the hypothesis already states.

page_size gate: decode's tests run page 64 by default (reference PAGE = 64), including 'batch 1, ctx 10, layer sliding' (SB1) and 'batch 8, ctx 2047, layer sliding' (SB16). A2's cluster kernel assumes one 128-byte row per token (page 1), as do attention's _sd_gate/_ps_gate/_slide_gate, which all require page_size == 1. Every A1/A2 cell gate must keep page_size == 1, num_kv_heads == 2, head_dim == 64, window == 2048 and rope_theta != 0. Master's _sliding_forward has no page-size gate, so the SB1 fallback must remain master's.

inv_freq: attention's _inv_freq memoizes in a module-global dict keyed by (theta, d, device). That is derived from config, not from inputs, so it is allowed. Prefer decode's own _inv_freq or a state-held tensor built in prepare, so no per-call allocation happens on a first-seen key during graph capture.
No per-call mutable state or global BLAS flags are involved (no cuBLASLt preference toggling), so the standing policy is satisfied as written.
Every key: the windowed sk and cluster kernels attend all max(0, seq-2047)..seq keys, and the hypothesis's checks include lens {1, 63, 2047, 2048, 2049, 80000} and planted window-edge keys. OK.
open_questions: Which A1 variant and grid does SV1 race: variant 5 as written, or attention's measured variant 4 at grid p8? Recommend a sub-race over {4, 5} x {p4, p8, sm}, entering the winner.

Which graph is timed in each band race? Require the qkv GEMM through the o-GEMM input, cold L2 before the qkv GEMM, with PDL neighbours as master captures them. Otherwise the conjecture about L2 reuse and nodes is untestable.

Should S3 c1-c4 be included so the run is literally C1 + race (clean A/B against same-day C1 on every row)? If not, the summary should drop the 'contains C1' framing and compare with C1 only on Sd1, Sd16, Sd32 and Sv1.

prepare() is called per state copy: can the race choose different winners for the two states? Print the decisions of both calls. If they differ, the profile rows mix paths, so report both rather than reading a single row.
SB1's expected gain of about 1.7% of the row is at the 1.02 threshold. Report the race margin even when master is kept, so a near-miss is not read as a refutation.
